thread:
deploy-bot: Helm upgrade gpu-operator -> v1.5.0 completed in eu-west1 (staging/dedicated pools). Some nodes are reporting driver/kernel mismatches.
`helm upgrade gpu-operator redwood/gpu-operator --version 1.5.0 --namespace gpu-system`
UPGRADE SUCCEEDED
node/gpu-node-23 NotReady kubelet: driver/kmod mismatch

maria: FYI seeing ~12 GPU nodes go NotReady in eu-west1. Several pods failing with NCCL init errors. Marking page.

ash: Got a sample pod log? `kubectl -n ml logs gpu-train-job-abc -c trainer`

maria: Log snippet:
```
2026-02-15T10:12:03Z NCCL WARN  transport/net_gl: Connection failed: -1
2026-02-15T10:12:03Z NCCL ERROR Failed to init NCCL: unhandled system error
```
Pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.

ravi-ml: This smells like the device plugin/operator started enforcing driver <> CUDA strictness. New device-plugin changes in recent charts enable strict driver matching by default (env var STRICT_DRIVER_MATCH=1). If kernel module major/minor differs we get node-level gating.

jeff-eng: We didn't pin driver versions for dedicated nodes in eu-west1 after the last maintenance. Node kubelet reports nvidia driver 525.85 but the operator's compatibility matrix expects 530.x for the CUDA images we're scheduling.

ash: Can we rollback the operator helm release while we validate drivers?

maria: Rollback would stop the new checks, but pods might still surface NCCL errors until drivers are aligned. Still good short-term mitigation to restore scheduling.

ravi-ml: Quick mitigation: flip the strict check off in the device-plugin daemonset until drivers are consistent. Example:
`kubectl -n gpu-system set env daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin STRICT_DRIVER_MATCH=false`
Then `kubectl -n gpu-system rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin`.

jeff-eng: Applying mitigation now (patching daemonset, restarting).

deploy-bot: Patch applied: set `STRICT_DRIVER_MATCH=false` on daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin, rollout started.

ash: Also kicked a helm rollback to v1.4.1 as a fallback: `helm rollback gpu-operator 1 --namespace gpu-system`.

oncall: Alert summary: 12 nodes NotReady, ~40 pods impacted across 3 clusters in eu-west1 (staging & dedicated). Moving to incident mode until nodes are back.

maria: After the daemonset patch I'm seeing nodes transition back to Ready gradually. Scheduling resumes for a subset of workloads. NCCL errors reduce but a few GPU kernels still mismatch for long-running drivers (module version mismatch).

jeff-eng: We'll need a two-part remediation: 1) a short rollback/disable strict checks (done), 2) coordinated driver rebuild/deploy: build drivers for kernel X.Y and test CUDA 11/12 compatibility matrix, then rolling-update node pool with new modules.

ravi-ml: Agreed. Also add an e2e test in CI for operator chart that verifies device-plugin vs driver version matrix to catch this on chart upgrades.

ash: Note on capacity: eu-west1 has limited spare GPU capacity — if we need a fast drain-and-recreate, we might temporarily burst to us-central1 (higher cap) which costs more. I'll open a short-term budget approval with finance.

oncall: Confirmed raid: rollback + daemonset patch restored most scheduling by 10:26Z. Remaining 2 nodes need manual node-reboot to reload kernel modules.

maria: Manual reboots scheduled for maintenance window 11:00-11:30Z. Creating infra ticket with driver build artifact and per-cluster pinning plan.

jeff-eng: After maintenance we'll publish an operator compatibility matrix in the runbook and pin helm chart upgrades behind a staged canary in eu-west1. Also add automated preflight check in our upgrade pipeline to compare node driver versions with chart expectations.

ravi-ml: Also propose CI rule: disallow operator upgrades that flip STRICT_DRIVER_MATCH to true without a corresponding driver rollout job.

maria: Thanks all. Will follow up with the infra ticket and the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

oncall: Incident cleared to monitoring, reopen if regressions appear.
